help.title: Feature Guide
help.intro: LearnOS is a local-first personal learning system: record attempts → leveled hints → active recall → spaced review → oral exams. All data stays on your machine; AI is an optional enhancement — every module degrades gracefully without it.
help.quick.b: ① Configure an AI endpoint in Settings (OpenAI-compatible; local Ollama works) → ② Practice in Bank or record problems in Wrongbook → ③ Review on schedule and rate honestly → ④ Test understanding with Oral exams → ⑤ Track trends on the Dashboard. Start each day from Today's Actions.
help.dashboard.b: Shows due counts, mastery, 7-day review pressure, retention curves and error-type distribution. Today's Actions is a unified study queue: due reviews → oral exam on a weak concept → wrongbook consolidation → bank practice, advanced item by item. Stubborn problems (wrong ≥2 times) get their own list. Global search: Ctrl+K jumps across problems/concepts/bank/docs.
help.bank.b: Practice by subject/unit with instant grading. Wrong answers can be moved into the wrongbook in one click (with stem and explanation); statuses: todo / wrong / recently correct. Bulk-import custom questions via JSON, or extract examples from textbooks with the Material Import Wizard.
help.problems.b1: When recording a problem, fill in the question, your own attempt, error type and trap notes — where you went wrong matters more than the answer. Photos are supported: AI recognition produces a draft (vision model required) that is saved only after confirmation.
help.problems.b2: Four hint levels guide step by step: 1 concept check → 2 direction → 3 framework → 4 full solution (with a redo-it-yourself nudge). Level-1 hints add diagnostic advice after a failed review. "Variants" generates 3 similar problems as a confirmed draft; AI tagging follows the same draft-confirm rule. The list supports card/table views (sortable columns) and saved filters (name a filter combo and switch in one click).
help.review.b: FSRS-6 by default (built-in; falls back to SM-2), scheduling reviews at the optimal forgetting point. Rate each recall: forgot / fuzzy / recalled / instant — the more honest, the better the schedule. The queue is priority-sorted: most overdue > weakest > with gaps, with same-topic interleaving; a daily cap in Settings prevents overload. Overdue reviews are rescheduled at half interval; "Estimate optimal retention" simulates the workload/knowledge trade-off from your own deck, and parameters can be trained with enough reviews.
help.oral.b: Pick a concept and the AI probes five rounds deep — can you explain it in your own words? Oral exams and hints automatically inject your learner profile (weak spots / frequent error types / goals), steering follow-ups toward your weak areas. Afterward, generate a spoken-card draft into the wrongbook. Feynman mode pairs with a self-review rubric: explain first, then score.
help.graph.b: A standalone page (More ▾ → Graph) visualizing concept hierarchy, prerequisites and mastery: green = mastered, yellow = learning, red = weak. Concepts support aliases (e.g. N2L = Newton's Second Law). The wrongbook's "Unlinked mentions" card scans problem text for concepts (including aliases) that appear but aren't bound — confirm in one click for more accurate mastery stats. Concepts can be added or deleted manually.
help.rag.b: Ingest textbooks/slides/notes (md/txt/pdf) from the workspace; hints and answers automatically cite your material (sources clickable). BM25/FTS5 search is supported; deletion is undoable. Scanned papers can be OCR'd in the OCR card.
help.material.b: At the top of the Material Library page. Upload an md/txt file (up to 100MB) or pick an ingested doc → choose targets (concept graph / questions → bank / detect exam paper) → AI extracts a draft → check items → import. Segmentation adapts to the configured model context; long texts are fully covered automatically (with a confirmation when many calls are expected). Nothing is written without confirmation; without AI, heading-based concept extraction still works.
help.exam.b: Enter your past papers (or auto-detect them with the wizard), link questions to your wrongbook, and the system scores readiness per topic: green ≥80% / yellow ≥60% / red <60%, with a priority list of weak spots.
help.subject.b: Switch the current subject at the top right; graph/bank/wrongbook/review are isolated per subject. Add custom subjects (Chinese display names supported) or delete empty ones in Settings → Subjects; built-in physics/chemistry/math cannot be deleted. Drop data/seed_concepts_<id>.json to preload a concept map for a new subject.
help.ai.b: Configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint in Settings (api_base / key / models; separate fast and heavy tiers). API keys never touch the database: environment variable first, then an AES-GCM encrypted keystore (master password), then session memory; logs are redacted automatically. If AI is missing or fails: hints fall back to local templates, variants to offline templates, recognition to attachment mode — core flows always work.
help.data.b: Export JSON from the Dashboard (problems + hints + reviews); import auto-backs-up the database first. A daily backup lands in backups/ (7 kept). The database is a single local learnos.db — copy it anytime to migrate.
mat.title: Material Import Wizard (textbook/paper → graph/bank/paper)
mat.hint: Upload an md/txt textbook or paper (up to 100MB), or pick an ingested library doc. AI extracts: concept graph, example questions (into bank), paper structure. Segmentation adapts to the model context you configure; long texts are fully covered automatically. Draft preview first — nothing is written until confirmed. Requires AI; without AI only heading-based concept extraction is available.
